Coopanion is a desktop pet named Coo that lives on the bottom edge of your screen. It wanders along the edge, chats with you in speech bubbles and listens while you hold the talk key. If you let it, it can also look at your screen, click and type to use the computer for you. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.

The interface comes in 11 languages: 简体中文, 繁體中文, English, 日本語, 한국어, Français, Deutsch, Español (Latinoamérica), Português (Brasil), Italiano and Русский. On first start it follows the system language, falling back to English, and you can change it later under Language on the Habits page. Coo talks to you in the same language. Translations other than Simplified Chinese and English are machine-made; PRs that fix them are welcome.

 

 Features

- Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, MiniMax, Zhipu GLM, Doubao, Baidu Qianfan and StepFun: pick one and paste an API key. You can also sign in with a ChatGPT account and use its ChatGPT plan.
- Hold the talk key and speak, or type. Coo answers in a bubble. Speech is recognized on your machine by default, or by a transcription service you set up.
- Coo remembers you. What it knows about you is written to PARTNER.md , and longer memories are organized by topic and date. When Git is available, every change Coo makes to its text keeps a history; Windows ships with Git, macOS and Linux use the one installed on the system.
- With your permission, Coo can look at the screen, click, type and switch windows. This is off by default and you decide when it asks first. It pauses as soon as you touch the mouse or keyboard, and talking with the talk key interrupts it.
- An icon over Coo's head shows when it is thinking, reading files, searching, writing or using the computer.
- Pick Coo or DeepSeek Chan , an animated whale girl with eight vendor color schemes and three outfits. Other figure packs are imported on the Dress up page; see the figure pack compatibility promise.
- Coo comes in several colors, including Nai Coo and five Cultist Simulator principles, and can wear a hat, animal ears or a halo, headphones, an earring or a bow, glasses and neckwear. The size of the pet, its bubbles and the text can each be adjusted.
- Ask Coo to remind you at a time of day or in a few minutes, and it sets an alarm.
- Install Worlds such as a QQ bot, a drawing room and small games from World extensions → Extension market .
- Export Coo and its bubbles as an OBS Browser source with a transparent background, to put it on a stream.

What changed in each version is in Releases.

 Install

You need:

- Windows 10 or 11 (x64), Windows 11 (Arm64), macOS 13 or later (Apple silicon or Intel), or a 64-bit Linux desktop (X11; in a Wayland session it runs through XWayland, with the limits under Linux; speech recognition needs glibc 2.32 or later, which means Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 or newer);
- an API key from one model service, billed by usage (see Cost and privacy), or a ChatGPT account with a plan.

Every release page has a SHA256SUMS.txt for checking the downloads.

 Windows

- Installer : download Coopanion-Setup- .exe from the latest release and run it. On a PC with an Arm processor, download Coopanion-Setup- -arm64.exe . The installer is not code-signed, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC": click More info → Run anyway . It installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Coopanion by default, and the program and its data both live in that folder. Don't install it into Program Files or another folder that needs administrator rights: Coopanion can't write its data there and quits with an error. Launch it from the desktop shortcut. If the installer could not create the shortcut, open Coopanion.exe in the install folder.
- One command : in PowerShell, run

 

 The script downloads the installer for your processor. If antivirus software blocks the graphical installer, the script keeps the downloaded installer and prints its path. Run the downloaded installer with /S for a silent install, or add Coopanion to your antivirus's allowed list and try again. A fresh silent install defaults to %USERPROFILE%\Coopanion .
- Portable : download Coopanion- -win-x64-portable.zip ( …-win-arm64-portable.zip for an Arm processor) from the latest release, unpack it anywhere and run Coopanion.exe . Its data is kept in the folder's data . Copy the whole folder and you have a second Coo with its own memory and settings; up to 5 can run at once, installed and portable together. The portable version does not update itself: unpack the new version into a new folder and copy the old data over.

 macOS

1. From the latest release, download Coopanion- -mac-arm64.dmg (Apple silicon) or …-mac-x64.dmg (Intel), open it and drag Coopanion into Applications.
2. The app is neither signed with an Apple developer ID nor notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch. Open it once and click Done on the warning, then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway and enter your password.
3. Coopanion's icon is in the menu bar. It shows up in the Dock only while the settings window is open.

While the App Store is in front, Coo drops behind other windows so it doesn't cover the Touch ID prompt for purchases.

install.title: Install
install.html:
You need:

  • Windows 10 or 11 (x64), Windows 11 (Arm64), macOS 13 or later (Apple silicon or Intel), or a 64-bit Linux desktop (X11; in a Wayland session it runs through XWayland, with the limits under Linux; speech recognition needs glibc 2.32 or later, which means Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 or newer);
  • an API key from one model service, billed by usage (see Cost and privacy), or a ChatGPT account with a plan.

Every release page has a SHA256SUMS.txt for checking the downloads.

Windows

  • Installer: download Coopanion-Setup-<version>.exe from the latest release and run it. On a PC with an Arm processor, download Coopanion-Setup-<version>-arm64.exe. The installer is not code-signed, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC": click More info → Run anyway. It installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Coopanion by default, and the program and its data both live in that folder. Don't install it into Program Files or another folder that needs administrator rights: Coopanion can't write its data there and quits with an error. Launch it from the desktop shortcut. If the installer could not create the shortcut, open Coopanion.exe in the install folder.

  • One command: in PowerShell, run

    irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pal-AI-Lab/Coopanion/main/installer/install.ps1 | iex

    The script downloads the installer for your processor. If antivirus software blocks the graphical installer, the script keeps the downloaded installer and prints its path. Run the downloaded installer with /S for a silent install, or add Coopanion to your antivirus's allowed list and try again. A fresh silent install defaults to %USERPROFILE%\Coopanion.

  • Portable: download Coopanion-<version>-win-x64-portable.zip (…-win-arm64-portable.zip for an Arm processor) from the latest release, unpack it anywhere and run Coopanion.exe. Its data is kept in the folder's data. Copy the whole folder and you have a second Coo with its own memory and settings; up to 5 can run at once, installed and portable together. The portable version does not update itself: unpack the new version into a new folder and copy the old data over.

macOS
  1. From the latest release, download Coopanion-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg (Apple silicon) or …-mac-x64.dmg (Intel), open it and drag Coopanion into Applications.
  2. The app is neither signed with an Apple developer ID nor notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch. Open it once and click Done on the warning, then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway and enter your password.
  3. Coopanion's icon is in the menu bar. It shows up in the Dock only while the settings window is open.

While the App Store is in front, Coo drops behind other windows so it doesn't cover the Touch ID prompt for purchases.

[!NOTE] macOS asks for Microphone (voice input), Input Monitoring (talk key), Screen & System Audio Recording and Accessibility (computer use) the first time each one is needed, and switching apps during computer use also asks to control "System Events". Restart Coopanion after changing Screen Recording, Input Monitoring or Accessibility. macOS does not carry these permissions over to an updated version: if a switch is on but Coopanion says the permission is missing, remove Coopanion from that list with −, add /Applications/Coopanion.app back and restart.

Linux
  1. From the latest release, download Coopanion-<version>-linux-x64.deb (Debian / Ubuntu) or Coopanion-<version>-linux-x64.AppImage (other distributions).
  2. deb: sudo apt install ./Coopanion-<version>-linux-x64.deb. AppImage: install your distribution's FUSE 2 compatibility library, run chmod +x Coopanion-*.AppImage, then start it.

[!NOTE] The pet is a transparent always-on-top window, so the desktop needs compositing (on by default in GNOME and KDE). The tray icon needs status icon support (GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension); without a tray you can still right-click Coo to open the settings. Computer use needs xdotool and zenity, which the deb pulls in; under Wayland, screenshots also need one of grim, spectacle, scrot or ImageMagick.

In a Wayland session Coopanion runs through XWayland, which sees the cursor only over X11 windows. While the cursor is over the desktop or a native Wayland window, Coo's eyes do not follow it, and the hover buttons show only once the cursor moves onto Coo.
